title: RAW UNREVIEWED: p-opening frames a case and y-opening introduces its treatment response
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Hypothesize a two-part practical handbook construction: a complete p-initial paragraph states a patient's condition or material case, and a complete y-initial paragraph supplies the operation/result that answers it. GDT1075 supplies a within-register paragraph-opening form contrast, but GDT1076 found NO_CAPACITY for same-base exact-follower similarity; this proposal uses neither follower count as evidence nor a repaired pairing. The whole unit is the full boundary-delimited p-opening paragraph and the full boundary-delimited y-opening paragraph in one already enumerated same-section/same-hand register, with all intervening positions retained; no target pair is selected now. Smallest interpretive consequence would be reading their relation as “given condition → response,” rather than two independent descriptions. Rival: p/y marks paragraph organization or a formal opening class without case/response meaning. Which paragraph identities pair, which words carry the clinical roles, and whether a source tradition supports this exact use remain unknown.

design.mechanism: A paragraph-level discourse constructor takes the p-initial unit as an input/case and the following y-initial unit as an answer or treatment; the semantic link crosses complete paragraph boundaries and is not a local prefix translation.
design.unit: One complete boundary-delimited p-opening paragraph and one complete boundary-delimited y-opening paragraph in the same section and hand from the GDT1075 register inventory, including every group between the two boundaries; no follower subset is admitted as a substitute.
design.contrast: Case-to-response discourse relation versus independent paragraph topics, rubrics, or formal p/y opening classes with no semantic cross-reference.
design.prediction: A plausible complete reading must state a case referent in the first paragraph, preserve that referent into the second, and give the second a response relation; if either whole unit requires unrelated participants or the pair is only lexical similarity, the proposed connection fails.
design.scope: Exploratory design only. GDT1076's capacity failure remains binding; this is not a rerun of its follower test and does not establish an eligible pair.
